plan.title: HFD vs chow mouse liver DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single-batch mouse liver bulk RNA-seq experiment: raw Salmon gene-level counts (12,000 mouse gene symbols x 12 samples) in counts.csv and a 12 x 2 metadata table giving one condition per sample (high-fat diet vs chow, 6 vs 6, unpaired). The research question has two parts — which genes change, and which hallmark pathways change — plus one explicit data-quality concern: sample_01 has a library size roughly 4x below the median.

The plan therefore starts with a QC/outlier adjudication step (T1S1) rather than jumping to DE. A 4x-low library is not automatically a bad sample: DESeq2's median-of-ratios size factors handle depth differences, and the real question is whether sample_01 is merely shallow (low depth, normal profile) or genuinely aberrant (shifted profile, low gene-detection, PCA outlier separate from its condition group). T1S1 answers this with size factors, detected-gene counts, sample-sample correlation, and VST PCA/hierarchical clustering, and emits an explicit keep/drop recommendation with the evidence behind it. Which condition sample_01 belongs to matters: if it sits in a group of 6, dropping it makes that group n=5 and is a real power loss, so the bar for dropping is a demonstrated profile distortion, not depth alone.

T1S2 runs the primary differential expression on all 12 samples with DESeq2 (negative binomial, Wald test, ~condition, chow as reference), independent filtering, BH FDR, and apeglm-shrunken LFCs for ranking. T1S3 repeats the identical contrast with sample_01 excluded and quantifies concordance — rank correlation of the shrunken LFCs, overlap of the FDR<0.05 sets, and any gene whose call flips. This makes the outlier decision auditable instead of asserted: if the two DE results agree, the shallow sample is harmless and the full-n result stands; if they diverge, that is reported as a caveat on every downstream claim. The full-12 result is designated primary unless T1S1 produced hard evidence that sample_01 is aberrant.

T2S1 answers the pathway half with fgsea on the MSigDB MOUSE hallmark collection — the mouse-symbol GMT is staged, so no ortholog mapping is needed and no human set file should be substituted. Ranking uses the full shrunken-LFC-ordered gene list (all tested genes, not a thresholded subset), which is the appropriate design for an n=6-per-group experiment where a hard FDR cut may leave few genes. With 12,000 genes and ~12,000 background, hallmark coverage per set should be reported so sets with too few detected members are not over-read. Expected biology for HFD liver — lipid/fatty-acid metabolism, xenobiotic metabolism, inflammatory and bile-acid signalling — is a sanity check on the result, not a target to confirm.

Caveats carried throughout: n=6 vs 6 is adequate for strong effects but underpowered for subtle ones; there is a single batch so no batch term is estimable; the counts matrix is pre-filtered to 12,000 genes, which is well below a full mouse transcriptome and means the GSEA universe is already restricted; and gene symbols may contain duplicates from Salmon transcript-to-gene collapsing, which must be resolved before building the DESeq2 object.
